subject.title: fix(cron): respect deliveryBestEffort in interim-message suppression guard

question: Should `deliveryBestEffort: true` override the descendant-aware stale-interim suppression policy and deliver interim-style text to the configured target?
rationale: The code currently treats this final suppression guard differently from two nearby best-effort guards, but the resulting behavior change can intentionally expose messages that existing jobs do not send today.

options.title: Define best-effort as deliver available text
options.body: Approve the PR direction and require focused live cron delivery evidence showing the interim text reaches its configured target.

options.title: Preserve interim suppression
options.body: Keep the current final guard unconditional and close the linked bug report with documentation of the distinct suppression policy.

options.title: Introduce explicit policy control
options.body: Design a separate documented delivery policy only if maintainers need both best-effort transport and interim-message suppression independently configurable.

recommendation.title: Define best-effort as deliver available text
recommendation.body: Approve the PR direction and require focused live cron delivery evidence showing the interim text reaches its configured target.

likelyOwner.reason: Their adjacent cron-delivery work is the strongest available evidence of familiarity with the delivery-state boundary.
